transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess... I’m here because I can’t let go of some things around my father’s death. People keep saying the hospital records and those donation emails all make sense, but when I look at the timestamps and missing attachments, and how certain people in the community avoid answering me... it doesn’t add up. It feels like someone is hiding what really happened.
Do you find yourself thinking about your father's death and the surrounding circumstances for more than a few hours a day?

Yeah... probably more than a few hours some days. I try not to, but I keep going back over the records and the emails. The timestamps, the missing attachments, the way some people dodge my questions... it just feels obvious to me that something’s being hidden about what happened to my father.
Do you believe that the hospital or someone in the community is intentionally hiding information about your father's death?

Yes. I mean... I can’t prove every piece yet, but it feels intentional. The records and those donation emails—people say they line up, but the timestamps and missing attachments don’t sit right with me. And when certain people won’t answer simple questions, it’s hard not to think someone’s hiding what really happened.
Do you think others, besides yourself, also believe that the hospital or community is hiding information about your father's death?

Not really... I mean, most people tell me it all lines up and I’m reading too much into it. But when I look at the timestamps and the missing attachments, and how some people won’t answer me straight, it seems obvious to me that someone’s hiding something.
Do you think your beliefs about your father's death are possibly mistaken, or do you feel absolutely certain that you are correct?

I guess people want me to say I could be wrong, but... no, not really. When I compare the timestamps and the missing attachments with how certain people avoid my questions, it seems obvious someone is hiding what really happened.
Has your investigation into your father's death and your beliefs about it affected your relationships with family or friends?

A little, I guess. My work’s been mostly okay... I still get things done. But with family, some relatives kind of steer away from talking to me now. They know I might bring up the records or what I think was covered up, so they avoid it.
Do you feel like your thoughts about your father's death are causing you a lot of distress?
I don’t know... it bothers me, obviously. I wouldn’t be looking into it if it didn’t. But I wouldn’t say it’s... ruining me or anything. It’s just there.
Do you feel compelled to continue investigating your father's death, even when you've already looked into it many times?

Yeah... I mean, I don’t sit there all day with it, but I do keep going back to it.

People say the hospital records and the donation emails line up, but when I look at the timestamps and the missing attachments, and then certain people won’t answer me straight... it’s hard to just drop it. It feels like there’s something there.

Do you think your beliefs about your father's death would change if you found out that all the missing information you're looking for was actually explained and accounted for by the hospital or the community?

If everything was really explained, I’d look at it, sure. But... I don’t think that’s what’s happening.

People keep saying the hospital records and the donation emails match up, but when I compare the timestamps and see missing attachments, and then certain people in the community avoid answering me directly... it doesn’t feel explained. It feels like someone’s still hiding what actually happened.
Do you think your beliefs about your father's death would be considered strange or unreasonable by most people?

Most people probably think it’s unreasonable, yeah. But I don’t see it that way.

I know everyone keeps saying the hospital records and the donation emails line up, but when I look at the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how some people avoid my questions... it seems pretty obvious someone’s hiding something about what happened to my father.
Do you feel like you're unable to control your thoughts about your father's death?
I don’t know if I’d say unable to control them. They come up, especially when something reminds me of it, but… I can still do other things. It’s just not something I can completely put away.
Do you think your beliefs about your father's death would be considered delusions by a mental health professional?

They might call it that, I guess. I don’t agree with it.

I know people keep saying the hospital records and the donation emails all match, but when I look at the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how certain people won’t answer me directly... it seems obvious someone’s hiding what really happened with my father.
Would you say that no amount of evidence or explanation could ever change your mind about what really happened to your father?

I wouldn’t say nothing could change my mind. But… people keep saying the records and the donation emails line up, and I just don’t buy that it explains everything.

When I compare the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how some of those community people avoid my questions, it still looks obvious to me that someone’s hiding what really happened.
Do you think any new information, no matter how convincing, could ever make you question your current beliefs about your father's death?

I mean… I guess if it really explained everything, I’d have to look at it. But I’ve already seen what they keep pointing to.

The records, the donation emails — people say they line up. But the timestamps don’t sit right with me, and there are missing attachments. And when certain people in the community avoid answering directly… it still seems obvious someone’s hiding what really happened with my father.
Do you think you will ever be able to completely accept the official explanation of your father's death?

Completely? I don’t know.

Everyone keeps saying the hospital records and those donation emails line up, but when I look at the timestamps and the missing attachments… and how certain people won’t answer straight… it still feels obvious to me someone’s hiding what really happened with my father.
Do you think you could ever change your mind about what happened to your father, no matter what new information comes out?

I don’t know. Maybe if something actually explained all of it.

But I’ve looked at what they keep showing me — the records, the donation emails — and the timestamps, the missing attachments, the way some people avoid my questions… it still seems pretty clear to me that something’s being hidden about my father’s death.
Do you think there is any possible evidence that could be presented to you that would completely change your beliefs about your father's death?

I mean… completely change it? I don’t know.

People already say the hospital records and donation emails prove it all lines up. But when I compare the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how some people in the community dodge my questions… it still looks to me like someone’s hiding what really happened with my father.
Do you think it's possible for you to be completely wrong about what happened to your father?

I suppose it’s possible in the abstract. But… honestly, no, it doesn’t feel like I’m wrong.

I know people keep saying the records and emails line up, but when I look at the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how certain people avoid answering me… it still seems obvious someone’s hiding what really happened with my father.
Do you think there is any circumstance under which you would completely accept that your beliefs about your father's death are incorrect?

I don’t really see what circumstance would do that, no.

I know everyone keeps saying the hospital records and those donation emails line up, but when I look at the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how some people avoid my questions… it still seems obvious to me that something is being hidden about my father’s death.
Do you think your beliefs about your father's death would change if an independent investigation found no evidence of wrongdoing?

I’d listen to it, I guess. But no… I don’t think it would really change things for me.

Everyone keeps saying the hospital records and the donation emails all match, but when I compare the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how certain people avoid my questions… it still looks like someone’s hiding what really happened with my father.
